content: Nystatin is a medication prescribed to treat fungal infections affecting the skin, mouth, vagina, and intestinal tract. It is important to note that antifungal medications like nystatin are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. Occasionally, nystatin may be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Nystatin is available in various forms, including oral tablets, liquid suspensions, lozenges (pastilles), vaginal tablets, vaginal creams, and topical formulations such as powders, ointments, and creams. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use nystatin exactly as directed, without altering the dosage or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. For lozenges, allow them to dissolve slowly in your mouth without chewing or swallowing them whole. Continue using the lozenges for at least 48 hours after the symptoms of your mouth infection have resolved. The liquid form of nystatin is typically used three to five times daily for mouth infections and three times daily for intestinal infections. Shake the bottle well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. For mouth infections, divide the dose between both sides of the mouth, swish it around for several minutes, and then swallow. Good oral hygiene, including proper denture care, is essential for treating mouth infections. For intestinal infections, simply swallow the measured liquid dose without holding or swishing it in your mouth. For skin infections, nystatin ointment or cream is usually applied several times a day. Wash the affected area thoroughly before applying a small amount of the medication, gently massaging it into the skin. Avoid contact with the eyes if applying the medication to the face. If using nystatin powder for infections on the feet, dust the powder inside your shoes and stockings as well as on your feet. For vaginal infections, nystatin vaginal tablets and creams are typically used once or twice daily. Non-pregnant women usually use the vaginal tablets for two weeks, while pregnant women may require treatment for three to six weeks before delivery. Continue using the vaginal tablets or cream even if symptoms improve after a few days. Insert the medication high into the vagina using the provided applicator, following the instructions included with the product. Unwrap the vaginal tablets just before use. After inserting the medication, wash the applicator with soap and warm water, and wash your hands promptly to prevent spreading the infection. You may use a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains but avoid using tampons, as they can absorb the medication. Do not douche unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using the vaginal cream or tablets even during menstruation. Before starting nystatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nystatin or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking nystatin, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Nystatin may cause side effects. For vaginal tablets, creams, or topical formulations, common side effects include itching, irritation, and burning. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. For oral tablets or liquid forms, severe side effects may include diarrhea, upset stomach, stomach pain, or skin rash. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store nystatin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep tablets and liquid at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Store nystatin powder, lozenges, and vaginal tablets or creams in the refrigerator, but do not allow them to freeze. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your response to nystatin. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable, so if symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor.
